description_for_human: Search and retrieve Macrobond economic and financial time series.

functions.name: fetch_all_vintages
functions.description:
Fetch the complete revision history for a single series.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's
explicit confirmation, re-call with confirm=true and the returned invocation_token.

Results are paginated over the vintages: `limit` per page (default 20),
selected by `page` (1-based). Read `total_pages` / `has_next`. Pages after
the first are served from the cached result — no new confirmation or quota cost.

functions.name: fetch_entities
functions.description:
Fetch entity metadata (without observation values). Use for Release entities or metadata-only queries.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's
explicit confirmation, re-call with confirm=true and the returned invocation_token.

Results are paginated: `limit` entities per page (default 20), selected by
`page` (1-based). Read `total_pages` / `has_next`. Pages after the first are
served from the cached result — no new confirmation or quota cost.

functions.name: fetch_nth_release
functions.description:
Fetch the nth release of series (0=first/initial release, 1=first revision, etc.).

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Useful for constructing real-time datasets using only initially-released values.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's
explicit confirmation, re-call with confirm=true and the returned invocation_token.

Results are paginated: `limit` series per page (default 20), selected by `page`
(1-based). Read `total_pages` / `has_next`. Pages after the first are served
from the cached result — no new confirmation or quota cost.

functions.name: fetch_observation_history
functions.description:
Get the revision history for specific observation dates within a series.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Shows how the value for each date changed across successive data releases.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's
explicit confirmation, re-call with confirm=true and the returned invocation_token.

Results are paginated over the observations: `limit` per page (default 20),
selected by `page` (1-based). Read `total_pages` / `has_next`. Pages after
the first are served from the cached result — no new confirmation or quota cost.

functions.name: fetch_series
functions.description:
Fetch time series data (dates and values) for one or more series by name.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's
explicit confirmation, re-call with confirm=true and the returned invocation_token.

Results are paginated: the confirmed fetch retrieves every requested series
once, then hands back `limit` series per page (default 20). Read `total_pages`
/ `has_next` and request later pages with `page` (1-based). Pages after the
first are served from the cached result — no new confirmation or quota cost.

functions.name: fetch_vintage_series
functions.description:
Fetch series as they were at a specific point in time (vintage snapshot).

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

Call with confirm=false first to preview (fetches nothing); after the user's

Results are paginated: `limit` series per page (default 20), selected by `page`
(1-based). Read `total_pages` / `has_next`. Pages after the first are served

functions.name: get_attribute_information
functions.description:
Get information about metadata attributes (verify they exist).

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

functions.name: get_instructions
functions.description:
Return all Macrobond usage rules — discovery (searching, identifying, ranking
and presenting series), retrieval (fetching observation values / vintages, the
confirm protocol) and branding (chart / table / report styling). Call this once
per session before working with the other tools, then follow what it returns.

functions.name: get_revision_info
functions.description:
Check if series store revision history and get available vintage timestamps.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

functions.name: list_attribute_values
functions.description:
List all valid values for a metadata attribute (e.g., Region, Frequency, Source).

Call this directly when you need canonical filter values; only fall back to
get_attribute_information if it reports the attribute is unknown.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

functions.name: render_chart
functions.description:
Render one or more Macrobond series as an interactive line-chart widget.

This is how you show trend data on a host that renders widgets — a chart the
user can hover and zoom, rather than a wall of numbers. The series must already
be confirmed (the user picked them in the series picker); rendering unconfirmed
series fetches nothing and returns an error naming them.

The chart has a single value axis: only combine series with comparable
units and magnitudes (e.g. all percentages, or all index levels). Mixing
scales (GDP in millions with unemployment in %) flattens the smaller
series into an unreadable line — render separate charts instead.

functions.name: render_series_picker
functions.description:
Show the user the search results and let them choose which series to fetch.

**This is how you present search results — not a markdown list.** Search first,
then name that search here along with the series you would pick. The rows are
rebuilt from it; you do not repeat them.

That is deliberate, and it is the difference between the picker opening in about
three seconds and about fifteen. Everything in a row except your recommendation
is already on the server, so writing it out again costs seconds of your own
output for data that would be identical either way.

Confirming a series charges UTS once and unlocks fetching it — any fetch tool,
any date range — for one hour. This tool fetches nothing itself; it only shows
the choice.

functions.name: render_table
functions.description:
Render one or more Macrobond series as an interactive table of observations.

Each row is a date; each series is a column — sortable and resizable, so this is
how you show exact figures rather than retyping them into markdown. The series
must already be confirmed (the user picked them in the series picker); rendering
unconfirmed series fetches nothing and returns an error naming them.

functions.name: search_entities
functions.description:
Search for Macrobond time series by text and metadata filters. Returns entity names and metadata.

Use 1-3 distinctive keywords in `text`, never a sentence (e.g. text="core PCE",
not "US core PCE inflation"); put country / frequency / source into
must_have_values (e.g. {"Region": "us", "Frequency": "monthly"}).

**Do not present these results as a list.** Read them, then open the picker on
this same search: `render_series_picker(search_id=<the search_id below>,
recommended=[names you would pick])`. That widget is how the user chooses.

Pass the `search_id` back, never the rows. Every field the picker shows is
already on the server from this search, so writing the rows out again costs
seconds of your own output for data that would be identical either way — and
the handle cannot be mistyped into a different search the way a query can.

Results are paginated over the full match set: `limit` (min 1, default 20)
is the page size and `page` (1-based, default 1) selects the page. The
response carries `total_count`, `total_pages` and `has_next` — read those
to decide whether to request the next `page`. `is_truncated` is true only
when Macrobond itself capped the match set, so total_count is then a floor.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.

functions.name: suggest_search_phrase
functions.description:
Get search phrase suggestions for a natural language query.

This is the one tool that takes natural language — use it to turn a vague
topic into search terms, then apply keyword discipline to the resulting
search_entities calls.

If unsure of Macrobond's usage rules, call get_instructions() first.
